ECE 6612

Firewalls, state and tunnels

From the figure to the concept

Fig. 1 shows a packet’s endpoint fields being compared with ordered firewall rules.

A company exposes a public website while keeping its database reachable only from approved inside services. Its firewall enforces which traffic may cross a boundary. A default-deny policy requires an explicit permission for new exposure; default allow requires an explicit restriction. Choosing the default determines what happens when a new service appears before a matching rule is written.

A packet filter compares protocol, source and destination IP addresses, source and destination ports, and any other configured fields with its rules. In a first-match policy, evaluate from the top and stop when a rule matches. Broad early rules can cover the same traffic as a later exception. If no explicit rule matches, apply the stated default. The exact processing semantics should be supplied in a rule problem.

A stateless filter decides from this packet and its rules. A stateful firewall records approved communication and checks later traffic against expected endpoints, protocol and state. A reply packet travels inward even when an inside client initiated the connection outward. Keep packet direction separate from connection initiation. Merely setting a TCP ACK flag is a weak substitute for validated connection state because an attacker can set header bits.

Port numbers are protocol conventions. Cooperative programs can put other data on a familiar port. Tunneling wraps inner traffic inside another protocol, such as carrying data in DNS messages. Deep packet inspection (DPI) examines payload structure as well as headers, using additional processing and protocol knowledge. Encryption limits inspection to what a middlebox can observe or legitimately decrypt. The chosen observation layer determines the available policy evidence.

A remote-access virtual private network (VPN) authenticates a remote peer and supplies a protected tunnel to a gateway. Access beyond that gateway still follows network and application policy. A compromised remote endpoint can use a valid tunnel, so endpoint trust matters. An application proxy terminates one application session and starts another, allowing application-aware checks at the proxy. Requiring that route is part of enforcing the policy.

Central enforcement simplifies consistent control, but the policy must match changing services and users. Restrictive boundaries reduce connectivity and can complicate peer-to-peer communication. Allowed traffic still reaches application code, and compromised inside systems may already occupy the trusted side. Firewall rules, host protection and application authorization therefore enforce different boundaries along the complete path.

Example

With first-match processing, put “allow TCP from 203.0.113.8:any to 192.0.2.20:443” before “deny TCP from any to 192.0.2.20:443” to permit that one source. Reversing the rules makes the broad deny settle its packet first. A stateful return rule separately permits only replies belonging to an approved tracked connection.

Sources and scope
  • C19 Network Access Control and DoS pp. 3–27: policy, ordered filters, state, tunnels, VPNs and proxies.
  • November 10 recording covers these network-access topics.
  • NIST SP 800-41: firewall technologies and policy.

Practice

1. A first-match firewall has: (1) deny TCP from any to 192.0.2.20:443; (2) allow TCP from 203.0.113.8:any to that service; default deny. Evaluate a packet from 203.0.113.8:52000 and propose the smallest order change that expresses the exception.

Write the packet fields, then stop at the first matching rule.

Rule 1 matches, so the packet is denied before rule 2 is reached. Placing the narrow allow rule before the broad deny permits that source while retaining the deny for other sources. The result depends on the stated first-match semantics.

2. A policy permits inside clients to start HTTPS connections. An HTTPS reply arrives inward. What information lets a stateful firewall treat it as an approved reply, and what limitation remains?

Separate packet direction, tracked connection endpoints and application content.

The firewall matches the packet to the recorded protocol/endpoints and expected connection state of the approved outbound flow. Its inward direction is consistent with a reply. The tracked state establishes permitted communication under that policy; application payload still needs its own security checks.
